title: Sample Lineage Integrity
description: Assesses contamination risk, cross-contamination, traceability, chain-of-custody, and labeling integrity across a sample's full lineage.

steps.prompt: Assess the contamination risk for this sample based on its lineage. Consider: shared equipment used across different chemistries or electrode materials, inadequate cleaning steps between uses, airborne contamination during glovebox or fume hood work, and whether any parent sample had a contamination event noted. Use this rubric — 1: no contamination indicators, clean lineage; 2: minor risk (shared equipment, well-cleaned, low-interference chemistry); 3: moderate risk (shared equipment with differing chemistry, cleaning adequacy uncertain); 4: high risk (contamination event noted in lineage, or incompatible materials share preparation steps); 5: known contamination or lineage includes a sample flagged as compromised. Cite specific samples or preparation steps from the lineage. List 3-5 concrete mitigations.

Evaluate cross-contamination risk between this sample and sibling or co-processed samples in its lineage. Consider: whether multiple samples were prepared simultaneously in the same batch, whether they share a common parent that could have been mislabeled, whether ionic species from one sample could migrate to another during co-storage, and whether electrode slurries or electrolytes were prepared in shared vessels without full cleaning. Use this rubric — 1: samples prepared individually, no co-processing risk; 2: co-processed in batch but procedures are well-controlled; 3: batch preparation with one ambiguous cleaning or separation step; 4: co-processing with documented risk of cross-contamination; 5: cross-contamination event recorded or samples are indistinguishable. Cite specific lineage nodes or batch records. Provide 3-5 mitigations.

Assess the completeness and continuity of the chain of custody from the root sample through to the current sample. Consider: whether every transfer, split, or derivation step has a recorded timestamp and operator, whether storage conditions between steps are documented, whether there are any gaps in the lineage tree where provenance is unknown, and whether the sample was ever outside the primary research group's custody. Use this rubric — 1: complete, unbroken chain with timestamps and operators at every step; 2: minor gap (one transfer undocumented, low-ambiguity context); 3: one significant custody gap where sample location or handler is unknown; 4: multiple custody gaps, identity of sample cannot be fully verified; 5: lineage is broken, sample provenance is unknown. Cite specific lineage gaps. List 3-5 mitigations.

Evaluate labeling integrity across the sample lineage. Consider: whether each sample has a unique, persistent identifier (barcode, alphanumeric ID) that matches the records, whether any re-labeling events are documented and explained, whether label format is consistent with the project naming convention, and whether any samples in the lineage share an ambiguous or duplicate ID. Use this rubric — 1: all labels unique, consistent, and traceable to records; 2: minor inconsistency (naming convention variation, no ambiguity); 3: one re-labeling event that is not fully explained; 4: ambiguous or duplicate label detected in the lineage; 5: labeling error that could result in sample mix-up. Cite specific sample IDs or labeling events. Provide 3-5 mitigations.
